Hookshot 
 
 

 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator.
 

 
 Features 
 Status 
 Install and play 
 In-game menu 
 Mods 
 Save editor 
 Problems 
 Build from source 
 How it works 
 Want to help? 
 Credits 
 License 
 

Documentation · Common issues and answers · Report a bug

Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows or Linux program,
the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens
 on your PC, from your own copy of the game .
 

 [!WARNING]
 Some users report the file in releases to be a Trojan - it is not. Feel free to run it through any antivirus software

Discord: 
 

 [!IMPORTANT]
 This repository does not contain the game, keys or an executable , and it does not explain how to get them. You
 need your own copy. Everything the build creates ( hookshot.exe , the generated code, the shader caches and your
 saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files.

 Features

 Runs natively 
- The game's own code, translated to C and compiled for your PC: no emulator. Windows (Hookshot Builder, one setup
 file) and Linux and Steam Deck (one AppImage).
- High frame rates (60, 90, 120, 144, 165, 240 or uncapped, and 30), with the game kept at real-time speed.
- Any screen shape: ultrawide, 16:10 and 4:3, with the HUD at the screen's edges or in the middle 16:9.

 Graphics 
- Upscaling and anti-aliasing: NVIDIA DLSS and DLAA, AMD FSR 4 and FSR 3.1, Intel XeSS, or none.
- Frame generation: DLSS Frame Generation (up to what your card allows) and FSR 3.1 frame generation on every GPU, with
 the HUD kept still.
- Render and output resolution, view distance (foliage, detail, grass, shadows), shadow resolution, anisotropic
 filtering, HDR, CRT monitor and TV filters, and a fullscreen monitor choice.
- An FPS counter with a frame-time graph and a details page; F12 saves a screenshot.

 Mods and saves 
- Mods : RomFS mods, ExeFS code patches and Atmosphère cheats, in the emulators' folder layout. Turn them
 on and off and put them in order on the in-game Mods tab or the Builder's Mods + Editor page. Mods that each
 grow files load together.
- Save editor : the Builder's Mods + Editor page edits your save: stats, inventory, story
 progress and every save entry, with a backup each time it saves.
- In-game tools on the Debug tab: the inventory editor, rupees, teleport, travel, switch age, free camera, no-clip
 flight, set time and more.
- Saves are backed up outside the game folder at every start and as you save, and come back if they go missing.

 Controls 
- Controllers and keyboard and mouse, with every control remappable (the ocarina notes too) and mouse look.
- Motion aiming with a controller's gyroscope, an item wheel, and item cycling.
- One Vibration setting for every controller: a DualSense on a USB cable plays the game's fine haptics through its voice
 coils, and Switch controllers get their own HD rumble.
- NFC : amiibo from your own dumps.

 Everything else 
- An in-game menu ( F1 ) drawn in the game's own style, in several languages.
- Audio output device choice, and a microphone test with level and gain for the ocarina.
- Crash reports from the game's own window, with your graphics card filled in.

 Project status

Experimental. Players have reported on many PCs, from Kokiri Forest to the dungeons: the table says what works and
what does not yet. Open problems are collected in tracking issues, linked below.

 What Status 
 --- --- 
 Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around ✅ Works 
 Sound, controller, keyboard and saves ✅ Works 
 In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling ✅ Works 
 Flicker (the picture flashing too bright while moving) ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 ( 645) 
 Ground fog vanishing when looking down ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 ( 638) 
 Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed 
 Stutter when entering new areas ⚠️ Still happens the first time you visit a place. The next visits are smooth 
 Performance ⚠️ Depends on the PC: some reach a steady 60 fps, others stay below it, more so in Hyrule Field 
 Hyrule Field, Castle Town, Kakariko and the dungeons ⚠️ Players got there, with open bugs: lighting and shadows ( 1004), crashes and freezes ( 2507) 
 Ultrawide and 4:3 ✅ Works. The Aspect ratio row's default, Monitor's shape, widens the 3D to the screen ( 2119); the HUD keeps its 16:9 size with its corners at the screen's edges, or in the middle 16:9 with the HUD layout row; movies stay in the middle 16:9 
 NVIDIA cards ✅ Works. The most tested 
 AMD cards ⚠️ Many tested: reports from the RX 6600, RX 6800 XT, RX 7800 XT, RX 7900 XTX and RX 9070 XT. On Windows, the RX 6000 cards (Navi 21 and 22) draw task and mesh shaders through the compute fallback by default, as the driver lost the GPU with them ( 1747, 1992, 2215). Driver crashes and device lost are still reported ( 996) 
 Intel cards ❓ Few reports, many of them black screens or crashes ( 999) 
 Cards without mesh shaders (such as AMD RX 5000 and older) ❌ Not supported: parts of the picture are missing. Since v2.0.6 a fallback runs the mesh programs as compute shaders on cards with buffer device addresses ( 640); it leaves out the mesh draws that take their count from a buffer 
 Linux ✅ Works with the AppImage. Tested on several distributions (CachyOS, Fedora, Bazzite, SteamOS) and cards, with open problems on some AMD cards ( 1000)

install.title: Install and play
install.html:
The game does not come ready-made: Hookshot Builder builds it on your PC from your copy. You do this once. After that you start the game from its launcher, which also updates it.

What you need
  • Your copy of the game at the supported version: program 0400486024DEC000, update v131072, build e0f3ccfa. Other versions do not work. A .nup file, a .nx file made from one (NXFormat's nxconvert pack-nup), or the romfs and exefs folders.
  • 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, or 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch, SteamOS ...) and a CPU with AVX2. The Linux AppImage needs AVX2; on Windows, and in a build from source, a CPU without it gets a game built for what it has, a little slower.
  • A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 series or newer, AMD Radeon RX 6000 series or newer, or Intel Arc. On Linux, Mesa or NVIDIA's driver. Cards without mesh shaders are not supported.
  • 8 GB of video memory (VRAM) or more is recommended. Cards with less can use the in-game menu's lower Quality presets.
  • 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB.
  • About 60 GB free while building, on an SSD if you can: a hard drive makes the build much slower. You can build on one anyway; the builder says so first.
  • An internet connection for the download. Nothing else to install: the builder brings its own compiler and tools.
On Windows

For a portable install on an external SSD, run the downloaded setup with --portable; see Portable Hookshot Builder for folder, move and repair behavior.

  1. Open the latest release and download HookshotBuilder.exe.
  2. Run it. It downloads the rest of Hookshot Builder (about 500 MB), checks it, and opens it.
  3. Pick your game. The builder looks for .nup and .nx files in your Downloads, Desktop and Documents folders and lists them under Found on this PC. Not listed? Press Browse…, drop the file on the window, or choose romfs and exefs folders. The builder checks that it is the right version.
  4. Under Install the game to, keep the folder (Games\Hookshot in your user folder) or press Change. Choose the Game language.
  5. Press Build the game. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory. You can use your PC in the meantime.
  6. When it says Your game is ready, press Play. The Desktop shortcut and Start menu entry boxes are ticked: untick them if you don't want them.

Next time, start the game from the Hookshot shortcut, or hookshot.exe in the game folder. That is the launcher: it has Play, and Update when a newer release is out.

The first start prepares the game's shaders, which takes a while. Later starts are faster.

On Linux
  1. Open the latest release and download Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage. It is Hookshot Builder with everything it needs inside.
  2. Allow it to run as a program. In most file managers: right-click it, open Properties, and turn on "Allow executing file as program" (the words differ between desktops). Or in a terminal: chmod +x Hookshot-*-x86_64.AppImage.
  3. Double-click it. The Hookshot Builder window opens.
  4. Under Game files, choose .nup file (a .nx file goes here too) or romfs and exefs, then press Browse to pick them. The builder checks the version.
  5. Under Save the game to, keep ~/Games/Hookshot or choose another folder. Choose a Language.
  6. Press Build. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory.
  7. When it says "Your game is ready", press Play.

The game is also added to your applications menu as "Hookshot". That entry, and hookshot in the game folder, open the launcher: Play, and Update when a newer release is out. Keep the AppImage where it is: the launcher uses it to update.

When the desktop gives the launcher its own systemd service, Play waits up to two seconds for the game's separate scope before closing the window. If that hand-off fails, it cancels that attempt before starting the game directly, and records the fallback in hookshot_startup.log after the game exits. A direct start still follows the desktop's original service lifetime; this fallback cannot bypass a desktop that stops its children.

The same AppImage also builds and starts the game without opening the window, for a machine you reach over SSH or for a script: see Linux, the AppImage from the command line.

For fast GPU memory imports on Linux, the game user needs read/write access to /dev/udmabuf (the kernel's udmabuf module). Without it, Hookshot falls back to host-pointer imports, which can be much slower on AMD/RADV (NVIDIA's driver refuses these dma-bufs, so on NVIDIA the game uses host-pointer imports, which are not slow there); permission errors produce a warning on stderr and in hookshot_log.txt. With an NVIDIA card on NVIDIA's own driver you do not need this access and can ignore that warning: the check runs at the start, before the game knows which GPU it has. Otherwise, check ls -l /dev/udmabuf and id. An administrator can add you to the device's owning group, then you must log out and back in. Only use that group if access to its other devices is intended: kvm also grants virtualization access. For an active local desktop session using systemd-logind, prefer a device-specific rule in /etc/udev/rules.d/70-hookshot-udmabuf.rules: SUBSYSTEM=="misc", KERNEL=="udmabuf", TAG+="uaccess" (before 73-seat-late.rules). This grants access to the active local user, not SSH or service users. For those, an administrator can instead create a dedicated udmabuf group, add only the game user, and use SUBSYSTEM=="misc", KERNEL=="udmabuf", GROUP="udmabuf", MODE="0660" in that file. Reload with sudo udevadm control --reload-rules and apply with sudo udevadm trigger --action=add /sys/class/misc/udmabuf; restart the session/service after a group change. If the device is absent, the distribution must provide/load the module first (sudo modprobe udmabuf). Do not run the game as root or make the device world-writable.

Updating

When a new release is out, the launcher says "Update available". Press Update: in hookshot.exe on Windows, or in hookshot (or the AppImage) on Linux. It downloads only the parts that changed and builds the game again in the same folder. The build files of the last build are gone by then (see Where the files go), so an update takes about as long as the first build. Your saves and settings are kept. What changed is on the Releases page.

What an update keeps and replaces, and updating from the command line

To be safe, copy your saves somewhere first: the user folder in the game folder on Windows, or ~/.local/share/hookshot on Linux.

Kept Replaced
Your saves (user, or ~/.local/share/hookshot on Linux) The game in bin and its files
hookshot_options.ini, the in-game menu's choices and your controls image.bin and the shader list
hookshot_env.txt language.txt, written again with the game's language
texts: the texts reworded for a PC, made again
mods
mods, and hookshot_mods.txt (the Mods tab's order and switches) exefs_patches.txt, written again with the ExeFS patches the build applied

The game files the first build read are kept in the game folder, so an update does not need your .nup again.

From a clone: git pull, then python -I nx2/make_game.py --update <game folder>. The Linux AppImage does the same with --update <game folder>.

Latest development build

Want a fix before it is in a release? The latest development build is made from main after every change, with the same files as a release. It is untested and may break your saves or settings: copy them first (see above).

  • Windows: download HookshotBuilder.exe from it and start it from a terminal as HookshotBuilder.exe --tag nightly (without --tag nightly it installs the latest release instead).
  • Linux: download Hookshot-<version>-x86_64.AppImage from it and use it as above.

To go back, install the latest release the usual way.
